summary: This React component displays a warning notice on blog posts older than one year. It pulls the publication date from the blog post metadata, checks if there's a recent update or review date that would make the content still relevant, and renders either a 'reviewed and accurate' notice, a generic 'outdated' warning, or nothing at all.

explanations.29: useBlogPost() is a Docusaurus hook that gives us access to the current blog post's information like its publication date and custom front-matter fields.
explanations.34: useDateTimeFormat is a hook that gives us a formatter object configured for the user's locale — we're passing UTC timezone because custom date fields in this blog are stored as UTC midnight.
explanations.43: The TypeScript 'as' keyword tells the compiler to treat this field as an array of update objects, since this custom field isn't part of Docusaurus's standard type definitions.
explanations.49: We're spreading the updates array and sorting it by date in descending order (newest first), then grabbing [0] to get the most recent update.
explanations.56: We create a new Date object representing 'now', which by default initializes to the current moment.
explanations.57: setFullYear subtracts one year in place — this gives us the date from exactly one year ago.
explanations.59: We compare the post date against one year ago; if the post is older, isOld becomes true.
explanations.67: If a review_date was provided and it's within the last year, we consider the post recently reviewed and show a positive notice instead of a warning.
explanations.75: role="status" tells screen readers this is a live status message that users should be aware of, rather than just decorative content.
